newsitem.title: JAPAN: SPEED SKATING-NEW SKATES HELP VELDKAMP AND DITTRICH.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-NEW SKATES HELP VELDKAMP AND DITTRICH.

text.p: Bart Veldkamp of Belgium and Germany's Frank Dittrich dominated the men's 5,000 metres at the world speed skating championships on Friday after switching to revolutionary new skates less than a month ago.
After two races, Ids Postma of the Netherlands held a slim lead of 78.269 points over Japan's Keiji Shirahata, whose third-place finishes in the 500 metres and 5,000 metres earned him 78.336 points.
American K.C. Boutiette was third overall with 78.792 points.

Veldkamp completed 12-1/2 laps of the high-domed M-Wave oval in six minutes 43.26 seconds wearing Dutch-made "slap" skates, whose blades release at the heel. Dittrich's time of 6:43.74 was a German record.
Six of the top 10 5,000-metre finishers wore the new skates.

Veldkamp, who skipped last month's European championships to compete in the Eleven Cities skating tour in the Netherlands, said the edge offered by the new skates left heavier competitors at a slight disadvantage.
"But it's not only the skates," said the Dutchman who began competing for Belgium two years ago. "You also have to be really fit."

The boot heel on the new skates rises from the blade when the skater pushes against the ice, permitting a more natural stride. But the mechanism that slaps the blade back to the heel has proved too weak for some heavier skaters.
Defending overall champion Rintje Ritsma of the Netherlands, one of the heaviest competitors at 94 kgs, said he tried the skates last year but found them unstable.
Competing on conventional skates, Ritsma placed ninth in the 500 metres and seventh in the 5,000 metres to stand fifth overall.
Sprint specialist Lee Kyou-Hyuk of South Korea won the men's 500 metres in 37.14 seconds, cheered on by thousands of flag-waving Japanese schoolchildren.
Postma was second in 37.36 ahead of Shirahata, who finished in 37.59 seconds at Japan's first covered oval, which will host speed skating events at next year's Nagano Winter Olympics.
Postma, who at 89 kgs also chose to compete on conventional skates, added an eighth-place finish in the 5,000 metres to take the overall lead.
Only one medallist in the women's 500 metres wore the new skates, which helped Dutch female skaters to produce sensational results on the World Cup circuit earlier this year.
Annamarie Thomas of the Netherlands sped to victory in 40.53 seconds after switching back to conventional skates following poor results at the last World Cup event in Hamar, Norway.

Thomas edged out defending overall world champion Gunda Niemann of Germany, who turned to the new skates in desperation after being beaten by Tonny De Jong of the Netherlands in six World Cup races this season.
The 30-year-old distance specialist was second in 40.79, her third-fastest career time.

"I was a little nervous about using the slap skates because I'd had problems with starts before," said Niemann, who was paired against De Jong. "Half my starts were good and half were bad. But it was a good decision to use them here."

American Becky Sundstrom, 1995 junior world champion, placed third in 40.89. World Cup leader De Jong, who also beat five-time Olympic medallist Niemann at last month's world championships, was sixth.
Competition continues on Saturday with the men's and women's 1,500 metres and the women's 3,000 metres.
